note: _hash01: one Python call per row of the int arrays a, b, c, d (as many as the call names); "phase" is the number its sine is taken of, sum(x * k for x, k in zip(xs, HASH_K)) + 0.5 (Python's sum() of floats is compensated, so this is not the plain left-to-right sum), and "out" what it returned. math.sin comes from the C runtime of the reference PC: a port with another sine can differ from "out" in the last bits, never from "phase". _sand_puff: t and tl are float.hex() strings, col null is col=None. args.canvas makes the picture the call draws on, w x h, uint8 RGB: with only "flat", that colour everywhere; with "mul" and "add", pixel i (counted row by row from the top left) has the channels (mul[c] * i + add[c]) % 256, and if "rows" [ya, yb] is there too only rows ya to yb - 1 are woven like that and the rest is "flat". "out" is the picture after the call.
